docs.title: Home
docs.text:
Beware and warning! This book is different from other books. You and you alone are in charge of what happens in this story!

Choose Your Own Adventure (1979)

The 21st century is known for its interactive art, where the boundaries between audience and performers are blurred thanks to the use of technology. However, such openness has also been part of experimental projects in the previous century. For example, so-called gamebooks were designed as interactive stories in which the reader could decide the fate of the characters by choosing narrative paths at the end of each section.

In A Gothic Gamebook, the audience will unfold the story of a young couple of lovers according to the tropes of early 19th-century Gothic literature. For each scene, the musicians perform music belonging to a corpus of Romantic German lieder. The music itself is full of references to magic, fantastic creatures, ghosts and horror.

This musical game is part of the artistic research project A Whirlpool of Imaginary Sounds led by Nicholas Cornia (nicholas.cornia[at]orpheusinstituut.be).

docs.title: Wat is this game about?
docs.text:
This musical game aims to emulate the tropes of European fantastic literature of the 19th century through the unfolding of a series of predefined storylines, determined by the audience. Each scene is accompanied by songs belonging to a musical corpus designed in advance by the performers.

In A Gothic Gamebook we have selected songs from the German musical tradition of the Romanticism, with compositions by authors such as Johannes Brahms, Robert and Clara Schumann, Hugo Wolf, Franz Schubert and Johanna Kinkel.

Contrary to the fantastic literature and gamebook genres, where the story is usually told from the perspective of a single main character, we have introduced the possibility for the audience to switch the narrative between two characters. By turning the spotlight on a different character, the audience takes a more directive stance rather than a first-person immersive one. Furthermore, the ability to jump from a storyline to another enriches the complexity of the story graph, incresing significantly the space of possibilities while keeping the number of scenes reasonably small.

This musical game aims to brigde the divide between audience and performers, providing a space for co-creation and distributed authorship for canonical Western classical music repertoire.

docs.title: Storypath example
docs.text:
During the music festival of Oddities & Rarities (website in Dutch), a première of A Gothic Gamebook has been performed on 30 November 2025 at Orpheus Instituut Ghent.

Four singers and two pianists have shared a corpus of more than 30 German lied scattered into 28 scenes of the musical gamebook.

We have explicitly chosed for gender-neutral names for the main characters, respectively Sasha and Rune, and secondary characters, the witch Ymir and the hermit Vanadis.

docs.title: Data and statistics
docs.text:
According to our statistics, available with corresponding simulation code in our GitHub repository, there are 294 possible storypaths given the designed musical gamebook structure available here. Furthermore, our average storypath is 10 scenes long with an average duration of about 1 hour for the performance.

The fields goes_to and comes_from provide the hierarchical information for each scene in the graph, while change_spotlight regulates the possibility for the audience to suddenly turn the attention to the other protagonist.

Music is recorded in a CSV tabular structure with metadata, such as composer and title, and timing in minutes. In a similar fashion is possible to provide a list of scenes via tabular data.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: Two young lovers, Sasha and Rune, are in extreme distress. The greedy tutor of Rune has decided to marry them to an old, rich bachelor without their consent.On the day of the arranged marriage, the two have planned to meet at an old milestone near an abandoned castle and escape together. Rune escapes from captivity and is seeking shelter in the abandoned estate, while Sasha has to cross the great forest by night in order to reunite with their beloved.

docs.title: Act I
docs.text: Our protagonists encounter a series of challenges, both natural and supernatural, during the long night following their escape. Finally, tired and proved by many sleepless hours, they embrace the realm of dreams.

docs.title: Act II
docs.text: Sasha is confronted with the primorial and misterious sorcery of the witch Ymir, while Rune finds shelter and support in the abandoned chapel of the lonely hermit Vanadis.

docs.title: Act III
docs.text: The events of the last hours have challenged both body and spirit of our protagonists. Shall their love overcome their vicissitudes, or will they be parted forever?

docs.title: Core mechanic
docs.text:
A round of the game can be defined by the following steps:

  1. A scene is portrayed to the audience with a short description.
  2. Music associated with the current scene is performed.
  3. If there are more than one possible paths, the audience votes in order to pursue a certain direction in the narrative.

docs.title: Voting
docs.text:
How many choices?

As a rule of thumb, we advice to vary between one to three choices. It is possible to combine choices that bring the current character's arc forward with turning of spotlight to the other protagonist.

Voting can be done by using online interactive presentation tools, or by just letting the audience rising their hands. The Game Master, or narrator, is responsible for pacing the voting phase: on one hand, they have to keep the flow of the performance, on the other they have to allow enough room for discussion between the audience.

docs.title: Storypaths design
docs.text:
The design of storypaths for A Gothic Gamebook can be a time-consuming process. The designer(s) should familiarize with the main tropes of the literary genre in order to evoke immersion and verisimilitude in the audience. It is possible to either start from a corpus of songs, or from a series of connected scenes. Either ways, ad-hoc adjustments have to be made by the designer(s) and performers during the rehearsal process.

In order to provide some inherent structre to the storypaths, we recommend to pace the scenes in three acts.

  1. Let the audice vote for which character will initiate the narrative. Afterwards,provide several options for the audience in order to turn the spotlight between protagonists.
  2. The narrative, and the number of possible scenes, reaches its climax.
  3. Narrow the possible paths until the final scenes are reached. We advise to provide at lest two possible finales.

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Arriving at a clearing, the feeble light of dawn reveals a noble steed. Although richly bridled, there is no trace of a rider. Perhaps the lonely rider has lost his way, or was captured by the king of elves? Carefully approaching the horse, Sasha is unnerved by the distant sound of singing female voices.

docs.title: Choices
docs.text: Option Question Goes to A The character ignores the distant singing sounds and walks away from the clearing. Meeting the Witch B Intrigued by the monotonous sounds, resembling the repetitive, yet mesmerizing, experience of church litanies, the character decides to dive again into the woods, eager to reveal the source of the singing. Witches' ritual

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Wandering through the graveyard, a lone sepulchre draws the attention of our character. A decayed statue depicting a knight in armour has suffered centuries of erosion; a shadow of its former glory. The epitaph on the tomb tells the tale of a nobleman of old, tragically departing from our world on the day of his marriage.

Witch's love enchantment B The character is charmed by the unnatural beauty of Ymir, desperately falling in love with them. Demons keep the lovers apart

Fair ladies and courtiers of a forgotten time entice Sasha to join them. Sasha forgets all of their worries and the memory of their beloved Rune is merely a distant echo.

docs.text: Sasha and Rune are finally reunited. There are no words to describe their endless joy. A bright future awaits them, and if they haven’t died, they are still living happily together. “Und wenn sie nicht gestorben sind, dann leben sie noch heute”.

docs.text: Rain has been falling incessantly since Sasha’s departure. The path is inaccessible, and Sasha has lost their way. Their only chance is to climb the nearest hill in order to attain a new sense of orientation. Fighting against the rain and wind, Sasha realises that the storm is intensifying.

docs.title: Choices
docs.text: Option Question Goes to A Regardless of the weather, Sasha stubbornly proceeds in their march through the woods. docs.text: After being hit by the pebble, the strange bird emits a sharp sound like a woman’s scream. Is it possible? Instead of a bird, Sasha is confronted by a furious witch with pale skin and scarlet curls. Shrieking curses in an unknown language, the figure approaches. Sasha runs away as fast as possible.
